questions.question: Which of the following is a benefit of global trade for consumers:

options.A: More variety at competitive prices
options.B: Elimination of all domestic businesses
options.C: Guaranteed higher wages for every worker

questions.explanation: More variety at competitive prices. Trade lets consumers buy goods from many countries, which increases variety and competition and often lowers prices. It does not guarantee higher wages for everyone, it increases rather than reduces choices, and many domestic businesses continue to compete and grow.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of global trade

questions.question: When balancing a checking account, a check that has been written but has not yet cleared the bank is called a(n)

options.A: deposit in transit.
options.B: outstanding check.

questions.explanation: Outstanding check. An outstanding check has been recorded in the account holder's register but does not yet appear on the bank statement. A deposit in transit is money deposited that the bank hasn't recorded yet, an overdraft occurs when spending exceeds the balance, and a service charge is a bank fee.

performanceIndicator.text: Balance a bank account

questions.question: The financial market in which short-term debt instruments that mature in one year or less are traded is the

options.A: commodities market.
options.B: capital market.

questions.explanation: Money market. The money market handles short-term borrowing and lending through instruments such as Treasury bills and commercial paper. The capital market deals with long-term securities like stocks and bonds, the commodities market trades raw goods such as oil and wheat, and the insurance market involves transferring risk for a premium.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain types of financial markets (e.g., money market, capital market, insurance market, commodities markets, etc.)

questions.question: After the central bank raises interest rates twice in six months, Pembrook Homes notices that fewer buyers are signing contracts for new houses. Why?

options.A: Buyers earn less interest on their savings
options.B: Rising rates make houses cheaper to build
options.C: Higher rates increase the supply of new homes
options.D: Higher mortgage rates raise monthly payments

questions.explanation: Higher mortgage rates raise monthly payments. Most home buyers borrow, so higher interest rates raise monthly mortgage payments and reduce how much buyers can afford. Rising rates do not lower construction costs or increase housing supply, and they actually increase, rather than reduce, the interest savers earn.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the economic impact of interest-rate fluctuations

questions.question: While researching an article, Devon finds a website that has no author listed, was last updated eight years ago, and is selling a product related to the topic. Devon should

options.A: look for a more current, objective source.
options.B: cite it as an expert source.
options.C: use the information because it is online.
options.D: copy the website's statistics into his report.

questions.explanation: Look for a more current, objective source. The missing author, outdated content, and commercial motive all suggest the site may be unreliable or biased. Devon should find a recent source from a credible, neutral organization. Being online doesn't make information valid, and using or citing this source could weaken his report.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify sources that provide relevant, valid written material

questions.question: In the finance industry, compliance refers to

options.A: developing new investment products.
options.B: persuading customers to buy more financial products.
options.C: calculating the interest on customer loans.
options.D: obeying the laws and rules that apply to the firm.

questions.explanation: Obeying the laws and rules that apply to the firm. Compliance is the function that makes sure a financial firm obeys regulations and its own policies, such as anti-money-laundering and consumer protection rules. Selling, product development, and loan calculations are important finance activities, but they are not what compliance means.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature and scope of compliance in the finance industry

questions.question: Ravi enjoys analyzing data, is comfortable with math and statistics, and wants to help insurance companies set premiums based on risk. Which finance career best fits his interests?

options.A: Actuary
options.B: Bank teller

questions.explanation: Actuary. Actuaries use math and statistics to measure risk, and insurers rely on their work to set premiums. Loan officers evaluate and approve loans, bank tellers serve customers at the counter, and mortgage brokers match home buyers with lenders. None of these focuses mainly on statistical risk analysis.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss employment opportunities in the finance industry

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of using technology in customer relationship management:

options.A: Handwriting all customer records in a notebook
options.B: Keeping customer complaints off the computer system
options.C: Sending automated birthday offers to loyalty members
options.D: Asking customers to repeat their information on every call

questions.explanation: Sending automated birthday offers to loyalty members. CRM technology can automatically use stored customer data to send personalized messages, such as birthday offers. Handwritten records, making customers repeat information, and leaving complaints untracked are inefficient and weaken relationships.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in customer relationship management

questions.question: Before opening an office in South Korea, the managers of Halcyon Software take a course on local business etiquette, including how to present business cards and which gestures to avoid. The company is addressing

options.A: tariff schedules.
options.B: cultural differences.

questions.explanation: Cultural differences. Cultural considerations include customs, values, and etiquette that affect how business relationships form in other countries. Exchange rates and tariffs are economic factors, and patents protect inventions. None of these involve gestures or business etiquette.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain cultural considerations that impact global business relations

questions.question: Kendra, a new bank employee, wants guidance from someone experienced as she plans her career. Which resource would be most helpful?

options.A: An office supply catalog
options.B: A competitor's annual report

questions.explanation: A mentor. A mentor is an experienced person who gives advice, feedback, and support for someone's career growth over time. A competitor's annual report, a single trade show booth, and an office supply catalog do not provide personal career guidance.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize resources that can contribute to professional development (e.g., trade journals/periodicals, professional/trade associations, classes/seminars, trade shows, and mentors)

questions.question: Which of the following is a guideline for writing professional emails:

options.A: Use emojis in messages to all clients
options.B: Write the entire message in capital letters
options.C: Use a subject line that describes the message
options.D: Leave the subject line blank to save time

questions.explanation: Use a subject line that describes the message. A specific subject line helps recipients understand and prioritize the email. All capital letters read as shouting, a blank subject line looks careless and may be ignored, and emojis are usually too casual for client communication.

performanceIndicator.text: Write professional emails

questions.question: Which of the following is a primary source of information about a public corporation's financial condition:

options.A: Its annual report filed with regulators
options.B: A post on an online investing forum
options.D: A television commercial for its products

questions.explanation: Its annual report filed with regulators. Public companies must file annual reports with regulators that include audited financial statements, making them a reliable source for investors. Online forum posts may be inaccurate or biased, commercials are designed to sell products, and an employee handbook covers workplace policies rather than financial results.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe sources of securities information

questions.question: Which of the following is a reason a person might choose a credit union instead of a commercial bank:

options.A: Credit unions do not offer savings accounts
options.B: Credit unions often charge lower fees
options.D: Credit unions are owned by stockholders

questions.explanation: Credit unions often charge lower fees. Credit unions are nonprofit cooperatives owned by their members, so they often return earnings through lower fees and better rates. They do offer savings accounts and loans, and it is commercial banks, not credit unions, that are usually owned by stockholders.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss considerations in selecting a financial-services provider

questions.question: A stock table shows that Arden Foods closed at $48.20 with a net change of -1.30. What was the stock's closing price on the previous trading day?
questions.explanation: $49.50. Net change shows how much the closing price moved compared with the prior day's close. A change of -1.30 means the price fell by $1.30, so the previous close was $48.20 + $1.30 = $49.50. Subtracting the change would give $46.90, which reverses the direction of the move, and $48.20 is today's close.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret securities table

questions.question: Before applying for an internship at a regional bank, Amara researches the bank's services, recent news, and values. This research will most help her

options.A: tailor her application and interview answers.
options.B: avoid sending a résumé.
options.C: negotiate a higher salary than full-time staff earn.

questions.explanation: Tailor her application and interview answers. Knowing about the employer lets Amara explain how her skills match the bank's needs and shows genuine interest. Research doesn't replace a résumé or interview, and interns are unlikely to out-earn full-time employees.

performanceIndicator.text: Utilize job-search strategies

questions.question: The email feature that sends a copy of a message to other recipients without the main recipient seeing their addresses is

options.A: Cc.
options.B: Reply all.

questions.explanation: Bcc. Bcc stands for blind carbon copy, which hides those recipients' addresses from others. Cc shows all copied addresses, reply all sends a response to everyone on the original message, and forward sends a message on to new recipients.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate basic e-mail functions

questions.question: On a pay stub, gross pay is the amount

options.A: withheld for federal income taxes.
options.B: earned before any deductions are taken out.
options.C: deposited in the employee's bank account.

questions.explanation: Earned before any deductions are taken out. Gross pay is the total earned for the pay period, such as hours times hourly rate. Net pay is what remains after deductions and is the amount deposited. Federal income tax withholding and health insurance premiums are deductions taken from gross pay.

performanceIndicator.text: Interpret a pay stub

questions.question: Simone hires a real estate agent to sell her condo. The agent learns a buyer would pay more but tells Simone to accept a lower offer so a friend can buy it. Which duty has the agent violated?

options.A: Loyalty
options.B: Reimbursement

questions.explanation: Loyalty. Agents owe their principals a duty of loyalty, meaning they must act in the principal's best interest rather than their own or a friend's. Obedience means following lawful instructions, accounting means tracking the principal's money, and reimbursement is a duty the principal owes the agent.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of agency relationships

questions.question: During a recession, Lindgren Appliances sees sales of high-end refrigerators fall by 30% while repair-part sales rise. What is the best explanation?

options.A: The company raised the price of repair parts
options.B: Shoppers are repairing instead of replacing
options.C: Consumers have more disposable income than before
options.D: Interest rates are usually higher during recessions

questions.explanation: Shoppers are repairing instead of replacing. When the economy slows, people cut back on expensive purchases and make what they have last longer, which increases demand for repairs. Disposable income usually falls in a recession, nothing suggests the company changed prices, and interest rates typically fall rather than rise during recessions.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine the impact of business cycles on business activities

questions.question: In a debtor-creditor relationship, the creditor is the party that

options.A: is owed money.
options.B: collects taxes on the loan.
options.C: guarantees the loan for someone else.

questions.explanation: Is owed money. A creditor lends money or extends credit and is owed repayment. The debtor is the party that owes the money. A guarantor promises to pay if the debtor doesn't, and taxes are collected by the government rather than the creditor.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of debtor-creditor relationships

questions.question: Owen owns a car worth $9,000 and has $3,500 in savings and $1,500 in a checking account. He owes $6,000 on his car loan and $1,200 on a credit card. What is Owen's net worth?
questions.explanation: $6,800. Total assets are $9,000 + $3,500 + $1,500 = $14,000. Total liabilities are $6,000 + $1,200 = $7,200. Net worth is $14,000 - $7,200 = $6,800. $14,000 is total assets alone, $7,200 is total liabilities, and $8,000 leaves out the credit card debt.

performanceIndicator.text: Determine personal net worth

questions.question: A clothing manufacturer publishes a yearly report showing its water use, carbon emissions, and waste reduction alongside its financial results. This report is an example of

options.A: variance analysis.
options.B: sustainability reporting.

questions.explanation: Sustainability reporting. Sustainability reporting shares a company's environmental and social performance with stakeholders, often alongside financial results. Variance analysis compares actual with budgeted figures, managerial accounting serves internal decision makers, and cash flow forecasting predicts future cash receipts and payments.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss non-traditional uses for financial information (e.g., lean, sustainability reporting, activity-based costing [ABC], six sigma)

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of currency:

options.A: A personal check
options.B: A five-dollar bill

questions.explanation: A five-dollar bill. Currency is the physical money issued by a government, such as coins and paper bills. Credit cards, checks, and gift cards are ways to make payments, but they are not currency themselves.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify types of currency (paper money, coins, banknotes, government bonds, treasury notes, etc.)

questions.question: The office manager at Holbrook Insurance notices the team uses about 10 boxes of copy paper a month and the supplier takes one week to deliver. To avoid running out, she should

options.A: buy a three-year supply at once.
options.B: set a reorder point.
options.D: order only after the last box is used.

questions.explanation: Set a reorder point. A reorder point tells her when to place an order so new supplies arrive before stock runs out, based on usage and delivery time. Waiting until the paper is gone causes a shortage, a three-year supply ties up cash and storage, and eliminating paper may not be practical.

performanceIndicator.text: Maintain inventory of supplies

questions.question: To show which sales regions are performing best, an analyst at Atlas Bank creates a map on which regions with the highest sales are shaded dark red and those with the lowest are shaded pale yellow. This visualization is a

options.A: pie chart.
options.B: line graph.

questions.explanation: Heat map. Heat maps use color intensity to show where values are higher or lower, which makes patterns easy to see at a glance. Pie charts show parts of a whole, line graphs show changes over time, and tables present exact values in rows and columns.

performanceIndicator.text: Use data visualization techniques (e.g., infographics, heat-maps, dynamic model outputs)

questions.question: Which of the following is a legal consideration that applies specifically to businesses in the finance industry:

options.A: Following rules that prohibit trading on inside information
options.B: Choosing a convenient location for the corporate office
options.C: Selecting a color scheme for the company website
options.D: Deciding how many tellers to schedule on Fridays

questions.explanation: Following rules that prohibit trading on inside information. Finance businesses are heavily regulated, and securities laws forbid buying or selling securities based on material, nonpublic information. Office location, staffing schedules, and website design are business decisions, but they are not legal requirements unique to the finance industry.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss legal considerations in the finance industry

questions.question: Jaylen has three credit cards with balances. Using the debt avalanche method, which card should he pay off first?

options.A: The card with the highest interest rate
options.B: The card he opened most recently
options.C: The card with the smallest balance
options.D: The card with the largest balance

questions.explanation: The card with the highest interest rate. The avalanche method focuses extra payments on the debt with the highest interest rate, which saves the most money on interest. Paying the smallest balance first is the snowball method, and the largest balance or the newest card is not the basis for either common strategy.

performanceIndicator.text: Control debt

questions.question: Darnell, an accounts payable clerk, notices that his supervisor has approved several payments to a vendor owned by the supervisor's brother-in-law without the usual bids. What is the most ethical action for Darnell to take?

options.A: Ask the vendor for a discount for himself
options.B: Report it through the company's ethics channel
options.C: Delete the payment records to protect the company
options.D: Say nothing because the supervisor approved the payments

questions.explanation: Report it through the company's ethics channel. Payments to a relative's business without competitive bids suggest a conflict of interest. Using the company's ethics hotline or reporting procedure lets the issue be investigated properly. Asking for a personal discount is itself unethical, deleting records is dishonest and possibly illegal, and staying silent allows potential misconduct to continue.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the role of ethics in financial-information management

questions.question: A U.S. retailer imports ceramic dishes from Portugal. The shipment is held at the port because the paperwork does not list the country of origin. Which area of regulation has the retailer failed to follow?

options.A: Customs documentation requirements
options.B: Product warranty and labeling laws

questions.explanation: Customs documentation requirements. Customs rules require accurate documents, including the country of origin, so officials can apply the right duties and trade rules. Missing information can delay or block a shipment. Fair labor standards, truth-in-lending, and warranty laws do not govern import paperwork.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of customs regulations

questions.question: Dividing a company's current assets by its current liabilities is a financial analysis tool used to measure

options.A: profitability.
options.B: productivity.

questions.explanation: Liquidity. The current ratio compares what a business can turn into cash within a year with what it owes within a year, showing whether it can pay its short-term bills. Profitability ratios compare profit with sales or assets, market share compares sales with the industry, and productivity measures output per input.

performanceIndicator.text: Demonstrate financial analysis applications

questions.question: Last year, Crestline Bank merged with Union Trust, and the combined company now offers checking accounts, insurance, and investment services to customers in five states. This merger is an example of

options.A: decentralization.
options.B: disintermediation.

questions.explanation: Consolidation. Consolidation occurs when financial firms combine through mergers and acquisitions, creating fewer but larger companies that often offer many services in one place. Decentralization spreads decision making out, disintermediation means customers bypass financial institutions, and risk diversification spreads investments to reduce risk.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the nature of convergence/consolidation in the finance industry

questions.question: During a team meeting about a new budget process, one member, Aiden, has not spoken. What could another participant do to encourage a balanced discussion?

options.A: Tell Aiden that his ideas probably aren't needed
options.B: Move on quickly before Aiden can respond
options.C: Speak for Aiden based on what he might think
options.D: Ask Aiden what he thinks about the proposal

questions.explanation: Ask Aiden what he thinks about the proposal. Inviting quieter members to share their opinions helps the group hear all perspectives. Speaking for Aiden assumes his views, rushing past him shuts him out, and dismissing his ideas discourages participation.

performanceIndicator.text: Participate in group discussions

questions.question: The financial-information management function is primarily concerned with

options.A: setting the prices of a company's products.
options.B: recruiting employees for the accounting department.
options.D: selecting the media for advertising campaigns.

questions.explanation: Recording and reporting financial data. Financial-information management covers how a business gathers, organizes, and reports financial data so managers, owners, and investors can make sound decisions. Pricing products is part of the pricing function, recruiting staff belongs to human resources management, and choosing advertising media is a promotion activity.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature and scope of the financial-information management function

questions.question: The process in which union representatives and management meet to reach an agreement on pay, benefits, and work rules is

options.A: collective bargaining.
options.B: a lockout.

questions.explanation: Collective bargaining. Collective bargaining is the negotiation between a union and an employer that results in a labor contract. Arbitration uses a neutral third party to settle a dispute, a lockout is when an employer keeps workers out, and a strike is when workers refuse to work to pressure the employer.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the concept of organized labor and business

questions.question: At Bramble Toy Company, one worker cuts the wooden pieces, another sands them, a third paints them, and a fourth packs the finished toys. Each worker performs only one task. The company is using

options.A: telecommuting.
options.B: job rotation among tasks.

questions.explanation: Division of labor. Division of labor breaks production into separate tasks assigned to different workers, which allows each to become faster and more skilled. Job rotation moves workers among tasks, telecommuting is working from a remote location, and outsourcing hires another company to perform work.

performanceIndicator.text: Analyze impact of specialization/division of labor on productivity

questions.question: A legitimate response to a customer's question is one that is

options.A: based on guesses when the answer is unknown.
options.B: long enough to fill an entire page.
options.C: accurate, honest, and relevant to what was asked.

questions.explanation: Accurate, honest, and relevant to what was asked. A legitimate response gives correct, truthful information that addresses the question. Length doesn't make a response better, changing the subject avoids the question, and guessing can mislead. If the answer is unknown, it's best to say so and find out.

performanceIndicator.text: Provide legitimate responses to inquiries

questions.question: Why do investors pay attention to a company's corporate governance?

options.A: Governance determines the color of the company's annual report
options.B: Good governance guarantees that the stock price will always increase
options.C: Strong governance reduces the risk of fraud and poor decisions
options.D: Companies with strong governance never pay dividends

questions.explanation: Strong governance reduces the risk of fraud and poor decisions. Effective governance, with independent oversight and transparent reporting, makes it less likely that managers will act against shareholders' interests. It cannot guarantee a rising stock price, has nothing to do with report design, and does not prevent a company from paying dividends.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the importance of corporate governance in business

questions.question: Which of the following is a good way to assess whether a career in finance fits your interests and skills:

options.A: Ask a friend to choose a career for you
options.B: Choose the career with the highest starting salary without learning about it
options.C: Take an interest inventory and talk with people who work in finance
options.D: Pick the first job listing you see online

questions.explanation: Take an interest inventory and talk with people who work in finance. Self-assessment tools and conversations with professionals help you compare what a career requires with what you enjoy and do well. Choosing only by salary, letting someone else decide, or picking a random job ignores your own interests and skills.

performanceIndicator.text: Assess personal interests and skills needed for success in business

questions.question: Which of the following is usually the most reliable source of information for a business report on unemployment rates:

options.A: A friend's opinion about the job market
options.B: A social media post from an unknown account
options.C: A blog post with no author or date

questions.explanation: A government labor statistics agency. Government statistical agencies collect data using consistent, documented methods and publish official figures. Anonymous social media posts, undated blogs, and personal opinions cannot be verified and may be inaccurate.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify sources that provide relevant, valid written material

questions.question: Before a civil case goes to trial, both sides exchange documents and question witnesses under oath. This stage of legal procedure is known as

options.A: sentencing.
options.B: discovery.

questions.explanation: Discovery. Discovery lets each side learn the evidence the other side has before trial, through documents, depositions, and written questions. An appeal asks a higher court to review a decision, a verdict is the decision at trial, and sentencing applies to criminal cases.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the nature of legal procedure

questions.question: A bias is a(n)

options.A: measure of employee productivity.
options.B: prejudice that can affect fair judgment.

questions.explanation: Prejudice that can affect fair judgment. A bias is a tendency to favor or disfavor something or someone, often without realizing it, which can lead to unfair decisions. A policy is a formal rule, a contract is a legal agreement, and productivity measures output.

performanceIndicator.text: Recognize and overcome personal biases and stereotypes

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of effective written communication in business:

options.A: It uses the active voice when possible
options.B: It avoids stating the main point

questions.explanation: It uses the active voice when possible. Active voice, such as "The team finished the report," is direct and easier to read than passive voice. Effective writing states the main point clearly, stays on topic, and is proofread so errors don't distract readers or hurt credibility.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of effective written communications

questions.question: Which of the following is a good practice for storing important business information for future use:

options.A: Using random names for every file
options.B: Backing up files regularly to a secure location
options.C: Keeping the only copy of records on a USB drive
options.D: Saving all files to the computer's desktop

questions.explanation: Backing up files regularly to a secure location. Regular backups protect information from hardware failure, theft, or accidental deletion. A cluttered desktop, a single USB drive, and random file names make information hard to find or easy to lose.

performanceIndicator.text: Store information for future use

questions.question: The owner of Fairway Auto Repair discovers that a replaced part was not needed. He calls the customer, explains the mistake, and refunds the cost, even though she never would have known. His decision demonstrates

options.A: price competition.
options.B: risk avoidance.

questions.explanation: Ethical behavior. Choosing to correct a mistake and refund the customer when no one would have found out shows honesty and fairness, which are ethical values. No law forced him to call, so it is more than compliance. The decision is not about competing on price or avoiding a business risk.

performanceIndicator.text: Explain the nature of business ethics

questions.question: Accounting software that automatically pulls transactions from a company's bank account and matches them to recorded entries helps businesses

options.A: reduce errors and save time on reconciliation.
options.B: set prices for their products.
options.D: eliminate the need for financial statements.

questions.explanation: Reduce errors and save time on reconciliation. Automated bank feeds and matching reduce manual data entry, which cuts errors and speeds up the process of reconciling accounts. Software does not remove a business's tax obligations or its need for financial statements, and it is not used to set product prices.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the use of technology in the financial-information management function

questions.question: A customer calls Midvale Bank asking why her account was charged a $35 fee. The representative does not know the reason right away. What should the representative do?

options.A: Suggest she close her account
options.B: Tell her all fees are final and cannot be explained
options.C: Transfer her to a random department
options.D: Look up the account to find the cause

questions.explanation: Look up the account to find the cause. Researching the account allows the representative to explain the fee accurately and, if appropriate, offer a solution. Refusing to explain, transferring without purpose, and suggesting she leave the bank are poor service that can cost the bank a customer.

performanceIndicator.text: Respond to customer inquiries

questions.question: At Kingsley Logistics, any purchase over $500,000 must be approved by the board of directors. When a manager wants to buy a new warehouse for $2 million, this governance rule means the manager must

options.A: split the purchase into smaller orders to avoid review.
options.B: ask the vendor to approve the purchase.
options.C: buy the warehouse and inform the board next year.
options.D: present the proposal to the board for approval.

questions.explanation: Present the proposal to the board for approval. Governance rules set approval thresholds so major decisions get proper oversight. The manager must take the proposal to the board. Buying first and reporting later breaks the rule, splitting the purchase to avoid review is deceptive, and vendors have no authority over the company's decisions.

performanceIndicator.text: Describe the impact of governance processes on decision-making and management functions

questions.question: Which of the following can affect a company's governance structure:

options.A: The brand of computers its employees use every day in the office
options.B: The laws of the country where it operates
options.C: The color of its delivery trucks
options.D: The flavor of coffee served in the break room

questions.explanation: The laws of the country where it operates. Governance structures are shaped by laws and regulations, ownership, company size, and industry. For example, public companies face stricter rules than private ones. Office equipment brands, break-room coffee, and truck colors have no effect on how a company is directed and controlled.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify the factors that impact governance structures

questions.question: Why is paper money accepted as payment even though the paper itself has little value?

options.A: It can be exchanged for gold at any bank
options.B: It is made from rare materials
options.C: It is backed by trust in the government
options.D: Each bill is backed by a share of stock

questions.explanation: It is backed by trust in the government. Modern paper money is fiat money, which has value because the government declares it legal tender and people trust it will be accepted. U.S. currency is no longer exchangeable for gold, bills are not made of valuable materials, and they are not backed by stock.

performanceIndicator.text: Identify types of currency (paper money, coins, banknotes, government bonds, treasury notes, etc.)

questions.question: Interest earned on most municipal bonds is attractive to many investors because it is

options.A: paid directly by the Federal Reserve.
options.B: guaranteed to double every five years.

questions.explanation: Exempt from federal income tax. Interest from most bonds issued by state and local governments is not subject to federal income tax, which can make a lower interest rate worth more after taxes. Municipal bonds do not double on a schedule, are paid by the issuing government rather than the Federal Reserve, and still carry some default and interest-rate risk.

performanceIndicator.text: Discuss the effect of tax laws and regulations on financial transactions
